question: What is the commercial status, pricing, and regulatory approval footprint of Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel)?
title: Casgevy: Global Approvals, Pricing Benchmarks, and Treatment Rollout

claims.text: Casgevy is the first CRISPR-based gene editing therapy approved by the US FDA for sickle cell disease (SCD) and transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia (TDT).
claims.reason: Directly backed by FDA press releases from December 2023 and January 2024.
supporting_quotes: FDA approved Casgevy, the first therapy utilizing CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing technology for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia.

claims.text: In the United States, Casgevy carries a wholesale acquisition cost (WAC) list price of $2.2 million per patient.
claims.reason: Exact price figure matches reported commercial pricing statements from Vertex Pharmaceuticals.
supporting_quotes: Vertex and CRISPR Therapeutics set the US list price for Casgevy at $2.2 million per one-time treatment.

claims.text: The European Medicines Agency (EMA) and UK MHRA have granted full marketing authorizations for both indications.
claims.reason: Confirmed by European and British regulatory agency notices.
supporting_quotes: Following MHRA authorization in late 2023, the European Commission granted conditional marketing authorization in February 2024.

claims.text: Over 10,000 patients received Casgevy infusions worldwide during the first six months of 2024.
claims.reason: The source clarifies that only dozens of authorized treatment centers were activated, with patient intake scaling gradually.
supporting_quotes: Patient cell collection and conditioning requires specialized authorized treatment centers (ATCs), resulting in gradual early adoption.

gaps_and_conflicts: Exact net reimbursement prices negotiated with EU national health payers (e.g. G-BA in Germany) remain confidential under statutory pricing agreements.
